input.quote: 18.1 This Agreement shall become effective on the date and year first above written and shall continue in operation for at least an initial period of twenty-five (25) years following the RFS Date (hereinafter referred to as "initial Period") and shall be terminable thereafter by agreement of the Parties. However, any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter by giving not less than one (1) year's prior notice thereof, in writing, to the other Parties.
input.rationale: Paragraph 18.1 sets a single 25-year initial period followed by open-ended continuation of the Agreement; there is no automatic renewal into fixed further terms and no renewal-linked price uplift anywhere in the Agreement (searches for renewal, notice and price-increase language return only the meeting-notice, amendment-notice and design-capacity-expansion provisions). Both fallback elements are therefore conditional on triggers that do not exist here: no automatic renewal means no non-renewal notice window to shorten, and no renewal price-increase mechanic means nothing to cap. The one (1) year's prior notice in 18.1 is not a non-renewal notice window but a standing unilateral exit right that each Party, including us, may exercise at the end of the Initial Period or at any time thereafter, so it operates in our favour and is not flagged; the same right is separately governed under the termination rules (18.2-18.4 and the withdrawal/asset-realisation mechanics), so we do not flag the term twice. We note only for the record that the evergreen structure means our exit requires 12 months' lead time, which is a term-length observation rather than a RENEWAL deviation. The clause therefore satisfies the fallback position on its material terms and we do not redline it to reach preferred renewal wording.
